text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] By sunrise, the whole city knew. The only problem… none of it was true. It started as one whisper at a food stall. The water is poisoned. Someone saw a stranger by the water tower last night. Nobody asked who saw him. Nobody asked how they knew. By seven, the shelves were empty. Mothers poured water down the drain. Old men argued at the mosque gate. And the story grew with every mouth it passed through. One stranger became three. Poison became a plan. By noon, they found him. A young man, new in the neighborhood. He had been fixing a leaking pipe… for free. The crowd closed in. Someone picked up a stone. Then the mosque speaker crackled. The water had been tested. It was clean. It always had been. The crowd went home. No one said sorry. No one asked who started it. The warning had been written long ago. And the Prophet said that repeating everything you hear is lie enough. That night, a new whisper began. This time, it named someone everyone trusted.
